candidates.mechanism: Weekly recipe-swap potluck in the empty room: residents bring one dish from their heritage, share its story and recipe, then exchange written copies. Two 90-minute sessions over two weeks.
candidates.answer: Mechanism: each session starts with a 10-minute welcome circle, followed by tasting and 3-minute story sharing per dish, ending with recipe cards exchanged. Participation: open to all 40 residents; volunteers handle room setup, sign-up sheet, and cleanup. Resources: 300 euros covers folding tables, tablecloths, printed recipe cards, and basic utensils. No specialist equipment needed; activity starts next Saturday.

candidates.mechanism: Same potluck structure but with a follow-up accountability loop: participants commit to cooking one new dish with a partner within a month, tracked via a shared photo wall in the town hall.
candidates.answer: Mechanism: first potluck identical to A; second session adds a matching board where people pair up and write a cooking date. Participation: same open invitation; volunteers manage matching board and reminders. Resources: 300 euros covers same items plus photo wall supplies and reminder postcards. Starts within two weeks, builds lasting pairs.

candidates.mechanism: Story-swap walking tour: volunteers map six short stops around town; pairs of residents trade personal memories at each stop, then reconvene in the empty room for tea. Starts next Sunday.
candidates.answer: Mechanism: pairs rotate every 12 minutes, guided by volunteer prompts; final 30 minutes in the room for group reflection and contact exchange. Participation: limit 24 residents, sign-up via library. Resources: 300 euros covers printed maps, name tags, tea, biscuits, and small notebooks. No equipment required beyond existing sidewalks.
